Quotes are crosstab rows copied from the Siena PDF with runs of spaces collapsed; each row lists Total first, and NYC is the 12th figure (after Total, Dem, Rep, Ind/Oth, M, F, Lib, Mod, Conserv, Union HH Yes, No). Column positions were read from the PDF's word coordinates, not by counting. polls.pollster: Marist Poll (Marist Institute for Public Opinion)
polls.mode: multi-mode: live-interviewer phone (273), text (923), online panel (252); sample from L2 voter file; English or Spanish
polls.notes: Results are Marist's likely-voter tables, which lead its release. Marist interviewed 1,448 registered voters (MOE 3.5) and applied a likely-voter weight; it did not publish the likely-voter count, so n is left blank and the MOE shown is the 3.9 Marist gives for likely voters. Registered-voter tables in the same PDF: governor Hochul 55% Blakeman 41% Another party's candidate <1% Undecided 4%; generic ballot Democrat 57% Republican 41%; Trump approval 37-62; Hochul favorable 43-48. nyc_results = crosstab row 'Region New York City' in the likely-voter tables; column order read from PDF word positions. Omitted as voting-behavior or survey-method items: VOTEREG1 (how often you vote), DUTY1/DUTY1R (duty vs. choice), CMPCT1 (campaign contact), NORMDESC1 (how many people you know will vote), SRCHMT26 (search-engine summaries). The release page blocks curl (Cloudflare), so every quote is a crosstab row from the tables PDF; '<1%' recorded as the string '<1', '0' as 0.

gaps.what: Research Co. (Vancouver) six-state online poll, Oct. 30-Nov. 1, 2026, 450 likely voters in New York, MOE +/-4.6, weighted by age and gender: governor Hochul 52%, Blakeman 43%, Undecided 5% (all 450); among 426 decided voters Hochul 55%, Blakeman 45%. The only New York question.
gaps.why_excluded: Held for Josh's call rather than added: an online-panel poll run across six states with no New York release, weighted only by age and gender (no party, education or region), from a firm that does not otherwise poll New York. It publishes its wording and tables, so it meets the letter of the methodology; adding it would also make it the newest poll on the page.

gaps.what: ActiVote New York governor poll, fielded Oct. 1-23, 2026 (median Oct. 12), 400 likely voters: Hochul 59.0%, Blakeman 41.0%; also attorney general James 56.5% and comptroller DiNapoli 58.5%.
gaps.why_excluded: Continuous opt-in poll of the app's own users (ActiVote's methodology page: it takes users' most recent recorded preferences over several weeks until it reaches 400); no question wording published and no undecided share reported.

gaps.what: Honan Strategy Group 5 Borough Barometer, Oct. 2-7, 2026, text-to-web, 967 likely NYC Democratic primary voters (269 Jewish, MOE +/-6): Mamdani job approval 73% overall; 2029 Democratic primary Mamdani 54% Tisch 17%; head-to-head Mamdani 54 Tisch 25, Mamdani 56 Menin 19; among Jewish voters Tisch 44 Mamdani 42 head-to-head, approval 45-51, 41% favor a second term vs. 44% time for someone new.
gaps.why_excluded: Numbers available only in news coverage reposted on Honan's site; no memo, toplines or question wording published. The sample is also likely Democratic primary voters, not all NYC voters.

gaps.what: Cornell ILR Empire State Poll 2026 (fielded June 24-July 8, 2026)
gaps.why_excluded: Still no 2026 report, toplines or questionnaire as of Nov. 2, 2026; the Empire State Poll page lists only the Sept. 11 news story for 2026 and the 2025 and 2024 reports. Remains left out.

gaps.what: Siena releases Oct. 12-Nov. 1 other than the Oct. 28 New York poll: NYTimes/Siena national (Oct. 21), Pennsylvania congressional districts (Oct. 25), Florida/Minnesota/South Carolina (Oct. 28), Nebraska (Oct. 31), seven-state likely voters and ReconMR Texas (Nov. 1); Marist's Oct. 14-27 releases cover Texas, Iowa, Ohio, Michigan, Maine and a national sample.

Quinnipiac, Emerson/PIX11, Suffolk CityView and Honan: no new New York City or New York State poll with full results released Oct. 12-Nov. 2, 2026 (Quinnipiac's latest New York release is Oct. 21, already recorded; Emerson's latest is Oct. 8; Suffolk's latest NYC CityView is Sept. 8).
